Definition: from G1909 and a derivative of G2672; imprecated, i.e. execrable:--accursed.
BiblicalUsage: Epikataratos means accursed, under a curse. Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things written in the book of the law to do them — and Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us.
TheologicalSignificance: The curse is real and the rescue is real, I believe: Christ took the curse so the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Him.
